MARTA KOWAL-BRANDT
DevOps / Cloud Infrastructure Engineer
Wroclaw, Poland | marta.kowalbrandt@example.com | +48 555 303 303 | gitlab.com/mkb-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
QA automation engineer with 7 years of experience, including the last two focused primarily on CI/CD, test infrastructure and build tooling. Owns GitLab CI pipelines and Helm-based ephemeral environments for three product teams. Personal infrastructure projects include a k3s homelab managed with Argo CD and Terraform-provisioned Hetzner VPS infrastructure. Brings a systems-oriented approach, analytical troubleshooting, and experience documenting CI processes and mentoring junior colleagues. Transitioning toward a full-time DevOps / platform engineering role.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Infrastructure & CI/CD: GitLab CI, Jenkins, Docker, Docker Compose, Helm, Terraform (personal project), Argo CD
Containers & Linux: Kubernetes (namespace-level access; Helm deployments to a shared cluster), k3s, Linux
Monitoring: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki; dashboards for test metrics
Programming & scripting: Python, Bash, Java (test code), SQL
Databases & testing: PostgreSQL, pytest, Playwright, Selenium, Postman
Cloud learning: AWS EC2 and S3 basics (personal learning); Hetzner VPS

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
QA Automation Engineer (Test Infrastructure) | Odrava Health Software, Wroclaw | 2021–Present
- Own GitLab CI pipelines for three product teams (~25 developers), covering build, unit, integration and end-to-end test stages, as well as artifact publishing.
- Reduced average pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes by profiling pipelines, parallelising test jobs, caching dependencies and separating end-to-end tests into their own stage; monthly CI runner costs fell by about 30%.
- Built short-lived merge-request test environments with Docker Compose and later Helm on the company’s shared Kubernetes cluster. Environments include the application, PostgreSQL and seeded data; they are automatically removed after merge or 48 hours of inactivity.
- Maintain a pytest and Playwright end-to-end suite of approximately 900 tests; reduced the flaky test rate from 7% to below 1%.
- Wrote Bash and Python tooling to seed PostgreSQL test data and built a Python/GitLab API workflow to collect test results for Grafana dashboards.
- Wrote an internal guide to how CI works, used in onboarding; mentored two QA interns in 2023.
- Work with namespace-level access on the shared Kubernetes cluster; the platform team operates the cluster.

QA Engineer | Brightmill Software House, Wroclaw | 2019–2021
- Tested web and mobile applications for client projects using manual and automated testing.
- Introduced a Java/Selenium automated regression suite for the largest client project.
- Configured Jenkins jobs for nightly regression runs.

Customer Support Specialist (2nd line) | Brightmill Software House | 2018–2019
- Investigated customer issues using logs and databases, reproducing bugs for developers.

SELECTED INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECTS
Homelab k3s Cluster with GitOps | Personal | 2024–2025
- Built a three-node Raspberry Pi 5 k3s cluster and deployed applications from a Git repository using Argo CD.
- Set up Prometheus, Grafana and Loki for monitoring, plus Traefik ingress and cert-manager for TLS.
- Provisioned infrastructure for a small Hetzner VPS with Terraform; used Ansible at a basic level.

Merge-Request Ephemeral Environments | Odrava Health | 2023–2024
- Implemented short-lived application and PostgreSQL environments deployed via Helm to a shared Kubernetes cluster from GitLab CI.
- Enabled QA and product teams to review features before merge and run end-to-end tests against each environment; environments are automatically destroyed after merge or 48 hours of inactivity.
- Technologies: GitLab CI, Helm, Kubernetes, Docker, Bash, PostgreSQL.

CI Pipeline Speed-up | Odrava Health | 2022
- Profiled pipelines across three teams, parallelised test jobs, added dependency caching and separated end-to-end tests into a dedicated stage.
- Reduced average pipeline duration from 38 to 14 minutes and monthly CI runner costs by about 30%.
- Technologies: GitLab CI, Docker, pytest-xdist.

Flaky Test Dashboard | Odrava Health | 2023
- Collected CI test results in PostgreSQL and created Grafana dashboards showing flaky tests by team.
- The flaky rate fell from 7% to below 1% after teams began addressing the most frequent failures.
- Technologies: Python, PostgreSQL, Grafana, GitLab API.

EDUCATION
BEng, Computer Engineering | Silesian Lowlands University of Technology | 2018

CERTIFICATIONS & PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT
ISTQB Foundation Level | 2019
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) preparation; exam booked for January 2027 (not yet passed)

LANGUAGES
Polish (native), English (C1), German (A2)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured CV with clear progression from QA automation into DevOps and infrastructure work. It uses measurable outcomes effectively, including reducing pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes, lowering runner costs by approximately 30%, and reducing flaky tests from 7% to below 1%. The professional summary is candid about the transition and accurately distinguishes company experience from personal infrastructure projects. The project section adds useful technical depth and makes the candidate's practical learning visible. The main content limitation is that several requirements of this particular cloud infrastructure role are either absent or only indirectly demonstrated, especially system design, networking, mTLS, security, Terragrunt, and production cloud operations. These are capability gaps rather than defects in the writing. The CV is professional and credible, with no detected unsupported certifications or experience claims.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is ATS-friendly: it uses conventional headings, readable text, standard chronology, explicit technology names, and no complex tables, graphics, or unusual formatting. Keywords such as GitLab CI, Kubernetes, Helm, Terraform, Docker, Linux, AWS, PostgreSQL, Prometheus, Grafana, and Argo CD are clearly searchable. Separating company experience from selected projects is also helpful for parsing and relevance. AI screening is likely to identify the candidate as a credible junior-to-mid DevOps or platform engineering transition candidate, particularly for CI/CD, test infrastructure, Kubernetes application deployment, and observability. Screening probability for this specific contractor role is lower because the CV does not show Terragrunt, mTLS, network design, security engineering, production AWS infrastructure, or full infrastructure ownership. The CV appropriately does not claim unsupported expertise in those areas.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns well with the role's infrastructure engineering, analytical thinking, observability, Linux, AWS-learning, and stakeholder-collaboration themes. It demonstrates ownership of CI/CD, ephemeral environments, Kubernetes application deployments, infrastructure automation through Terraform in a personal project, monitoring, documentation, mentoring, and enabling QA and product teams. These also support Corvale's ownership-oriented and collaborative engineering culture. However, the candidate's material shows important gaps against the role's stated must-haves: strong Terraform and Terragrunt, system architecture and system design, networking including mTLS, practical security awareness, and operating cloud infrastructure at the level expected for a contractor shaping a production platform. The candidate also lacks evidence of IoT, automotive, or remote-device integration and of backend/full-stack development beyond Java test code. AWS is present only at basic personal-learning level. The CV presents the transition honestly, but the role appears substantially more senior and infrastructure-focused than the candidate's documented experience.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR, HIGH-VALUE IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary, replace the final sentence, "Transitioning toward a full-time DevOps / platform engineering role," with a more role-relevant but equally accurate statement such as: "Targeting a DevOps / platform engineering role focused on CI/CD, Kubernetes application environments, infrastructure automation, and observability." This keeps the transition truthful while foregrounding the strongest match to the job.
2. In the Technical Skills section, change "Terraform (personal project)" to "Terraform (personal Hetzner infrastructure project)" and retain the qualification. This makes the scope immediately clear and avoids implying professional Terraform ownership.
3. In the Technical Skills section, change "Cloud learning: AWS EC2 and S3 basics (personal learning); Hetzner VPS" to "Cloud: AWS EC2 and S3 basics (personal learning); Hetzner VPS infrastructure provisioned with Terraform (personal project)." This uses the ad's AWS terminology while preserving the candidate's actual level of experience.
4. In the Professional Experience section under Odrava Health Software, revise the bullet beginning "Built short-lived merge-request test environments" to explicitly include the stakeholder outcome already supported by the project material: "Built short-lived merge-request test environments with Docker Compose and later Helm on the company's shared Kubernetes cluster, enabling QA and product teams to review features and run end-to-end tests before merge." This better demonstrates bringing stakeholders along.
5. In the Professional Experience section under Odrava Health Software, revise the documentation and mentoring bullet to make technical leadership more visible without overstating authority: "Authored the internal guide to how CI works, used for onboarding, and mentored two QA interns in 2023." The current wording is acceptable, but this version is more direct and ATS-readable.
6. In the Selected Infrastructure Projects section, keep the explicit limitation in the Homelab project, but change "used Ansible at a basic level" to "used Ansible for basic configuration tasks." This is more concrete while remaining truthful.
7. In the Certifications & Professional Development section, retain the statement that the CKA exam is not yet passed, but format it as: "Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) preparation — exam scheduled for January 2027; not yet certified." This reduces the risk that an ATS or recruiter interprets CKA as an earned certification.
8. In the Technical Skills section, retain Kubernetes' scope qualification, but make it more compact and searchable: "Kubernetes (namespace-level access; Helm deployments to shared cluster; no cluster administration)." This preserves an important credibility detail and prevents overinterpretation of the experience.

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is clear, well structured, professional, and substantially stronger than a conventional QA-focused CV for a DevOps transition. It uses quantified results effectively: pipeline duration reduced from 38 to 14 minutes, runner costs reduced by approximately 30%, and flaky tests reduced from 7% to below 1%. The experience and project sections provide credible evidence of CI/CD ownership, ephemeral environments, Kubernetes usage, observability, scripting, and analytical troubleshooting. The explicit clarification that Kubernetes access is namespace-level and that the platform team operates the cluster is particularly important and protects the document from overstating seniority. The main content limitation is that the CV presents a strong DevOps transition profile but not yet a strong match for a contractor expected to design and operate cloud infrastructure independently.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is ATS-friendly: it uses conventional headings, chronological experience, readable bullet points, standard text formatting, and relevant keywords such as GitLab CI, Kubernetes, Helm, Terraform, Docker, Linux, Prometheus, Grafana, Python, Bash, PostgreSQL, and AWS. The project section adds useful keyword density without relying on unsupported claims. AI screening probability is medium to high for junior or mid-level DevOps/platform roles, but lower for this specific contractor role because the CV does not contain Terragrunt, mTLS, networking, security, system design, or production cloud operations keywords supported by the candidate's background. Terraform is correctly qualified as a personal project, and the CKA entry correctly states that it is not yet passed.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns well with the role's analytical, ownership, CI/CD, Linux, observability, and collaborative engineering aspects. It shows hands-on infrastructure-related work through Helm-based Kubernetes environments, GitLab CI, Docker, Terraform-based Hetzner infrastructure, and a k3s homelab. The CV also demonstrates technical-topic ownership through pipeline ownership, internal documentation, mentoring, and enabling QA and product teams to review environments. However, the candidate's material indicates gaps against several core requirements: strong Terraform and Terragrunt, independent cloud environment design and operation at the required contractor level, systems architecture and system design, networking including mTLS, practical security, production on-call, and IoT or remote-device integration. AWS is present only at a basic personal-learning level. The document should not imply production cluster administration or on-call experience, because the source information explicitly says the platform team operates the cluster and the candidate has not been on production on-call.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR, HIGH-VALUE IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary, make the existing technical-topic leadership more prominent by changing the final sentences to something such as: "Owns CI/CD and test-infrastructure improvements across three product teams, documents technical processes used for onboarding, and mentors junior colleagues. Delivered measurable improvements in pipeline performance, environment provisioning, and test observability." Keep the final transition statement truthful, for example: "Transitioning toward a full-time DevOps / platform engineering role." Do not describe independent production infrastructure ownership or on-call responsibility.
2. In the Technical Skills section, add "Infrastructure as Code (IaC)" as a category or keyword associated with the existing "Terraform" entry, for example: "Infrastructure as Code: Terraform (personal Hetzner VPS project), Ansible (basic)". Do not add Terragrunt, because it is not present in the candidate information.
3. In the Professional Experience section under Odrava Health Software, make the stakeholder impact already documented in the Projects section visible in the main employment bullets. Add a truthful bullet such as: "Enabled QA and product teams to review merge-request features and run end-to-end tests in isolated environments before merge." 4. 6. Retain the qualification in the Kubernetes skill and the explicit platform-team ownership statement. Do not change the CV to claim that the candidate ran the Kubernetes cluster, administered production infrastructure, or handled on-call; the current wording is appropriately truthful.
